newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS-Call buying in T-bonds after futures' drop.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Call buying in T-bonds after futures' drop.

text.p: U.S. debt market participants bought calls on Treasury bond futures Monday in the wake of Friday's sharp decline in the underlying market.

One bond floor analyst said those who bought out-of-the-money calls could be looking for a quick rebound in bond prices but more likely were hedging long exposure in bond futures or another debt instrument.
Another options trader said he was planning to take profits by closing out short at-the-money call positions set before Friday's two-point sell-off in futures.
September bond futures slightly extended Friday's loss to close at 114-21/32, down 5/32 on the day.

Implied volatilities for bond options were little changed Monday after retreating Friday following the release of U.S. July employment and national purchasing managers' data. The stronger than expected statistics on employment and business activity threw bond futures into a tailspin.

Volatility for September bond options, which expire in about three weeks, edged down to 7.50 percent by the end of the session Monday after opening around 7.70 percent. December ended at 8.65 percent, down from 8.70 percent on the open.

Among the larger transactions in bond options, a Wall Street dealer bought 3,000 December 116-00 calls delta neutral against futures at 114-16/32, another dealer bought 1,000 September 115-00 calls, and a trading house bought 1,000 September 118-00 calls, floor sources said.
A third dealer was a seller of 3,000 December 120-00 calls.
Eurodollar volatility levels also stabilized from Friday, when, unlike bond vols, they shot higher in reaction to the plunge in futures prices.
"We got a big change in trend and it finally paid to own some options," said one Eurodollar analyst on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
December volatility was pegged at 9.25 percent in the 94 strike, with March 94.00 straddles at 11.04 percent.

The analyst forecast volumes would slip back slightly after this week's quarterly Treasury refunding of three- and 10-year notes and 30-year bonds and with futures expected to look for a new trading range.
Eurodollar floor traders said one investor was a particularly aggressive seller of puts during the session, selling 9,000 of the December 93.50/93.75 spreads and 2,000 December 94.00 puts outright.
